summary: Backend-only regression + live HTTP verification for Timeline V2 Phase-4 plug-ins 4 & 5 (LifeCycleTimingEngine, LifeMilestoneTimingEngine). All 47/47 pytest unit tests pass (test_life_cycle_and_milestones.py, test_transits_and_zr_engines.py, test_timing_evidence_layer.py, test_annual_profection_engine.py). All 7/7 live HTTP tests against Pete's public preview URL pass: engines_run == ['annual_profection','transits','zodiacal_releasing','life_cycle','life_milestones']; life_cycle ACTIVE with saturn_return window 2025-08-30 → 2028-08-29, confidence=high, age_years≈57.7, next_hit populated; scrubbed to 1978-06-01 returns active_windows=[] with populated next_hit (years_from_now>0) and age~10; life_milestones inactive for Pete with confidence=conditional and 'Record...' meaning; annual_profection/transits/zodiacal_releasing all still shape-compatible; /api/timeline/profection/current and /api/timeline/profection/series still return 200. No issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: Router prefers .get('life_events') and .get('recognition_moments') on the user doc and merges into extras.events — matches engine's data contract; empty case correctly yields active=False, confidence=conditional.

life_cycle_timing_engine.compute always returns active=True even for the quiet-stretch case (no active_windows). Router uses aggregator include_inactive default=False; since engine hardcodes active=True, the engine will always be surfaced. Behavior is intentional per code but note: an evaluator reading only `active` may misinterpret a quiet stretch as 'in a window'. Consumers should check details.active_windows length. Not a bug — flagging as observation only.
In life_milestone_engine._parse_iso, ev.get('date') accepts str/datetime/date; good. Nothing to fix.
